shouldFix.title: The normalization-duplicate fixture remains non-discriminating because its NFD member independently triggers the non-NFC rule
detail: The advertised byte edit is present: entrypoint bin/entry is a committed file, so the fixture no longer triggers the unrelated ENTRYPOINT_ABSENT clause.

schemas.v11 nevertheless enumerates two separate TC-PATH requirements and RJ-3 triggers: non-NFC path bytes, and Unicode-normalization duplicate paths. The v4 fixture pairs NFC bin/café with NFD bin/café. The latter is not NFC, so the same bytes independently violate the non-NFC requirement as well as collapsing to the first path under NFC normalization.

RJ-3 has no subcodes and the catalog expects only RJ-3. An implementation that validates each path is NFC but never checks pairwise uniqueness after normalization rejects these bytes and passes the fixture. The corpus therefore still cannot prove the normalization-duplicate requirement, even though the particular entrypoint mask from v3 is gone. The note and honesty repair calling the NFC/NFD pair the 'sole RJ-3 violation' collapse two separately listed requirements into one.
shouldFix.impact: This is the exact-byte class schemas.v11 specifically requires for Unicode-normalization duplicates. At the SATISFIED-grade bar, a fixture that a materially incomplete validator passes does not discharge that member, so CLAUDE-V3-S1 is only partially repaired.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Resolve the underlying observability problem in an authorized schema successor, then issue corpus v5 with new bytes rather than editing frozen fixtures. For example, define an exact normalization relation that permits two individually valid paths to collide (if compatibility normalization is intended), or give RJ-3 a required discriminating datum/subcode and precedence that proves the normalization-duplicate arm ran. Until then, record this class as blocked on that schema clarification rather than scoring a bare RJ-3 rejection as proof of both members.
